intent: vendor preset "Rising Embers" (Smoke and Fire) — validate against its thumbnail

iterations.critique: The render has the essential upward motion and orange-on-black ember coloration: between t1 and t4 the particle field clearly rises. However, it reads as a thin, sparse vertical string of tiny dots rather than the fuller, turbulent rising ember plume suggested by a Smoke and Fire "Rising Embers" preset thumbnail. The emission is too narrowly constrained, particles are too small, and there is little visible fiery glow or variation in the plume silhouette.

The render now has a denser orange ember field and clearly rises between t1 and t4, with a more convincing spread than the prior thin string. It still reads primarily as evenly soft glowing dots in a narrow, segmented vertical column rather than a cohesive turbulent ember plume. The particle scale remains small, and the motion/silhouette needs more lateral turbulence and a broader fiery core to better match a Rising Embers Smoke and Fire preset thumbnail.

The render now has a substantially fuller orange-on-black rising ember field, and the t1-to-t4 change clearly communicates upward movement. The broadening at the upper portion is more plume-like than prior iterations. However, it still reads as a collection of uniformly circular, soft orange bokeh dots rather than a turbulent Smoke-and-Fire ember plume: the center lacks a concentrated fiery source/core, particle paths remain fairly orderly, and the very high feathering makes the embers overly diffuse.

The orange-on-black palette and strong upward displacement from t1 to t4 communicate rising embers, with a denser central source than earlier attempts. However, the t4 field expands into a very broad, almost explosive spray that reaches/crops at the top edge rather than retaining a tapered vertical plume. The particles remain uniformly round glowing dots; the 30 feather makes their edges too bokeh-like and prevents a sharper, hotter ember appearance. The intended Smoke-and-Fire look needs a more concentrated lower core and a more coherent upward column with only moderate lateral drift.

The orange-on-black palette, dense lower source, and strong t1-to-t4 upward travel clearly communicate rising embers. At t1 the field is a reasonably coherent vertical cluster, but at t4 it still blooms too widely at the top and is cropped by the frame edge, reading more like an upward explosive burst than a sustained tapered ember plume. Individual particles remain large, uniformly circular glowing dots rather than sharper, varied hot embers.
